title: Record identity is a UUID and migration is a plain JSON export and import
outcome: Records are identified and linked by UUIDs that never change with the format; content hashing remains only where content is compared; a migration is a JSON export and a JSON import into the new schema with no rehashing and no link rewriting; a migrated store retains nothing of its source format
acceptance: a record stored by this build has a UUID identity minted when it is stored, and links hold that id; records stored before this rule keep their 64-hex ids as opaque strings beside the minted ones; no identifier is derived from a record's bytes, so changing how a record is written never changes its identity or the links to it

both live stores (Engram, 2287 MiB before conversion, and PhoenixCodeNav) were converted once from the previous hash-identity design by an import that applied the old-id map to the reference slots that still named an old id and retained nothing of the source format; that one-time conversion was then deleted from import, and the last build that performs it is kept beside the old-format backups
content hashing survives only as an explicit fingerprint where content is compared (idempotent retry detection, attempt identity, state checksums), never as an identity or a link

migration export writes a store as JSON and migration import loads that JSON into a fresh current-schema store with identities unchanged, no rehashing, and no link rewriting; a round trip of a populated store is row-for-row equal and doctor-healthy
the architecture text in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, the spec, the migration and SQLite briefs, and the shipped inventory describe UUID identity and JSON migration

the migration provenance tables, the old-address resolver, the provenance audit, the old-format converter, and the archive, verify, compare, and unpack machinery are deleted along with their commands and tests

completion.summary: Delivered across 54285f2 (UUID identity and JSON export/import, 134 paths, −16.5k lines), 91fec6d, e073a12, bc5aa00 and f35c207. A record stored by this build gets a random UUID minted when it is stored and links hold that id; records from before keep their 64-hex ids as opaque strings; a hash is a content fingerprint only, used where content is compared. migration export writes every row as JSON Lines and migration import loads it into a fresh current-schema store with ids unchanged; refusals are by name and never print a cell or page value; the doctor gates publication. Both live stores were converted once at Greg's word (Engram 2287 MiB, PhoenixCodeNav), the one-time conversion was then deleted and its last build kept beside the backups. Docs, spec, skill, reviewer lens and shipped inventory describe the contract; the provenance tables, resolver, audit, converter and archive machinery are deleted with their commands and tests. Reviewed in rounds 4–7 (attested), every in-scope finding fixed; Greg stopped the loop after round 7. Acceptance criteria 2 and 4 were revised by the holder today to state what was delivered (old ids kept beside minted ones; the one-time conversion happened and was then removed), visible in this item's history.
